description_en: The Vatsalā Mandira is actually a shrine of a protective deity (pīṭha) that stands on the banks of the Bagmati river southeast of the Paśupatinātha Mandira. The temple dedicated to Goddess Vatsaleśvarī, who is taken as one of the nine goddesses who serve as a shield to Paśupatinātha (Hasrat 1970, p. 25). chronicles refer to the temple as ‘Ādi Mūlapīṭha’ (lit. the first mainpīṭha) (Devamālāvaṃśāvalī2013, p. 36). The term Vatsalā comes from a Sanskrit wordvātsalya, which means ‘affection’.Nepāla-māhātmya, a collection of legends on sacred places and deities of Nepal, explains about the naming of the deity: Once, Lord Śiva abandoned his abode in Kailāśa, the mountain, and, in the form of an animal (paśu), roamed around the Śleṣamāntaka jungle with the name Paśupati. Fellow gods including Brahmā pleaded him to return to Kailāśa but refused to do so. As Śiva seemed determined not to return to Kailāśa, his wife Pārvatī also decided to live next to him on the banks of the Bagmati river. Śiva, then, named his wife Vatsalā in acknowledgement of hervātsalya(affection) for him (Acharya 1992, p. 19).The two-tiered temple has brass sheets laid on its roofs with a gilded finial safeguarded by a parasol (chatra) on top. An oblong narrow banner (patāḥ) hangs from the finial down to the lower roof. Of the total 24 struts below the two tiers, the ones under the lower roof contain statues of Bhairava accompanied by erotic carvings below him. There is an entrance without door leaves on all four sides of the sanctum on the ground floor; the northern one among them holds significance as the main entrance. It is said that it has no door leaves so that the goddess, as is her wish, might better inhale the odor of corpses, and the Bhasmeśvaraliṅga, over which an (invisible) umbrella of ash (bhasman) is said to hover (Michaels 2008, p. 27). Each entrance is adorned with an ornate wooden arch (toraṇa) on top, featuring a carving of Mahiṣāsuramardinī (lit. the slayer of the buffalo demon) at the center. Thesetoraṇas embellish the eastern, western, and northern entrances. The southerntoraṇa, on the other hand, showcases a figure of Cāmuṇḍā as the main deity. Inside the sanctum, Goddess Vatsalā is enshrined in the form of a plain circularyantra(a geometrical figure used as a tool for tantric worship and meditation) on a stone lotus.Chronicles state that Goddess Vatsalā was present in the Paśupati area at the time of the manifestation of Guhyeśvarī. She was enshrined in the form of an esotericyantraof stone by offering a human sacrifice during the reign of King Śivadeva in 206-205 BC (Kaligata Era 2895-96). Two or three years later, Paśupatinātha invited various goddesses, such as Bhadrakālī and Kaṃkeśvarī, from Kathmandu and founded the tradition of worshipping Vatsalā with a human sacrifice.Naraśivās, people who act like jackals by walking on all fours, would make noises as the worship took place. Later, during the reign of King Viśvagupta in 80 CE (Kaligata Era 3181), special worship was performed to appease Vatsalā to replace the annual human sacrifice with an unblemished black he-goat (Devamālāvaṃśāvalī2013, pp.36-37). Another chronicle recounts that King Śivadevavarmana let human sacrifices be performed for Vatsalā, knowing that she is the principal deity among thepīṭhas of Nepal. He also established the tradition of feeding a group of virgin boys and girls on the 13th lunar day of Caitra, and lighting an uninterrupted fire (akhaṇḍāgni) at the Mahādeva shrines of the entire city on the 14th of the dark fortnight of Caitra (Piśācacaturdaśī), and the chariot of the goddess to be carried around in a procession (Nepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī2016, 12.136-137). Besides these accounts, there is no historical record of the temple’s initial construction. There is, however, a large stone inscription set on the rear wall of the Pañcagaṇeśa Mandira north of Vatsaleśvarī. The fully-eroded inscription related to the Vatsalā Mandira probably belongs to the Licchavi period. Other historical records from the temple document the endowment of over 45ropanīs of land to set up a trust to perform various rituals at the temple in 1675 CE (NS 795) (M. Panta VS 2055, pp.43-44). Likewise, King Raṇabahādura Śāha offered the horns of a wildarnābuffalo for fermented beer (thvã) to be poured from it on to the stoneyantrarevered as Goddess Vatsalā (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2056, p.290). Another record relates to the offering of a bell to Vatsalā by Ṭhākuraprasāda Ṭaṇḍana Lāhurī Kṣetrī and his wife in 1911 CE (VS 1968) (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2056, p. 111). The 1934 earthquakes did not render any damage to the temple (Devamālāvaṃśāvalī2013, p. 37). In 2017 CE (VS 2074), the Chaudhary Foundation in cooperation with the Pashupati Area Development Trust renovated the temple and furbished it with colors.TheNepālamāhātmya, a scripture recounting the legends of sacred places and deities of Nepal, states that worshipping and receiving the blessed view (darśana) of Vatsalā, after purifying oneself with a bath in the holy Bagmati river, will grant devotees a place in Kailāśa, the divine abode of Lord Śiva. The scripture also emphasizes offering sincere reverence to Vatsalā to attain divine perfection (siddhi) (Acharya 1992, p. 19). At the temple, there is no separate priest appointed; instead, the daily rituals are performed by the Karmācārya priest of Jayavāgīśvarī (PPK1222) following the tantric tradition. The caretaker (dyaḥpāḥlāḥ) of the temple belong to the Khaḍgī community, the butcher caste. The temple observes thejāpāygu(lit. paint with cooked rice) ritual annually on the 14th of the dark fortnight of Caitra as part of the Vatsalājātrā (Michaels 2008, pp. 79-107). During this occasion, Vatsalā in the form of a stoneyantrais covered with threepāthīs of cooked rice, leaving only the tip visible. Additionally, unblemished black he-goats are sacrificed. On the same night, a tradition of feeding virgin girls and boys a grand feast of 84 dishes (caurāsīvyañjana) is also observed. On the new moon day of Caitra, Vatsalā is bathed with locally brewed beer made from fermented rice (thvã), which is discharged through the horns of a wild buffalo offered by Raṇabahādura Śāha. The ritual, known locally aschāhaykegu, involves using a small conduit (PPK0224-005) on the retaining wall by the river east of the temple to let thethvãflows. The drink is considered holy and people gather below the conduit to bathe in the sacredthvã. A member of the Dhvaṃ Guthi (lit. jackal trust) then howls like a jackal thrice. The Dhvaṃ Guthi, as recorded in Guṭhī Saṃsthāna (VS 2071, p.41), possesses over 31ropanīs of land.
description_ne: पशुपतिनाथ मन्दिरको दक्षिण-पूर्वमा बागमती नदीको तटमा वत्सला मन्दिर अवस्थित छ । अहिले तल्ले शैलीको मन्दिरको स्वरूपमा निर्माण गरिएको भएपनि मूलत: यो पीठ हो । पशुपति क्षेत्रका शक्तिपीठहरूमध्ये वत्सलेश्वरी पीठ ज्यादै महत्त्वपूर्ण शक्तिपीठ हो । पशुपतिनाथलाई आवरणको रूपमा घेरेर बसेका नौजना देवीमध्ये वत्सला पनि एक हो (Hasrat 1970, p.25) । वंशावलीमा यसलाई 'आदि मूलपीठ' भनिएको छ (Devamālāvaṃśāvalī2013, p.36) । 'वत्सला' शब्द संस्कृतको 'वात्सल्य'बाट आएको हो । नेपालमाहात्म्यमा वत्सलाको नामकरणबारे लेखिएको पाइन्छ । भगवान् शिव कैलाश पर्वतलाई छोडेर पशु रूप लिएर पशुपति नामबाट पवित्र बागमती नदीको तीरमा रहेको श्लेषमान्तक वनमा बसिरहेका थिए । ब्रह्मादि देवताहरूले हात जोडेर कैलाशमा गई बसिदिन आग्रह गर्दा पनि शिव मानेनन् । आफ्नो पति कैलाश पर्वत नफर्कने भएपछि पार्वतीले पनि शिवजीसँगै श्लेषमान्तक वनमा बस्ने इच्छा गरिन् । शिवजीको वात्सल्यले बागमती किनारमा बसेकी हुनाले शिवले पार्वतीलाई 'वत्सला' नाम राखिदिएका थिए (Acharya 1992, p.19) ।बागमती किनारमा रहेको यो मन्दिरमा दुई तहको पित्तलको छाना रहेको छ । छानामा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको गजूर राखिएको छ । गजूरमाथि छत्र ओढाइएको छ । मन्दिरको उत्तरपट्टिको मोहडामा गजूरदेखि तल्लो छानासम्म पुग्ने गरी पता: झुण्ड्याइएको छ । छानाको भार थाम्न माथिल्लो र तल्लो छानामा गरी जम्मा २४ वटा टुँडाल राखिएका छन् । तल्लो छानाको टुँडालहरूमा भैरव कुँदिएका छन् र टुँडालको तल्लो भागमा रतासनमा रहेका नरनारीका आकृति कुँदिएका छन् । यस मन्दिरको गर्भगृहको चारै दिशामा ढोका राखिएका छन्, तर चारै ढोकामा खापा नराखी खुल्ला राखिएको छ । ती चार ढोकामध्ये उत्तरपट्टिको ढोकालाई मुख्य ढोका मानिन्छ । चारैवटा ढोकामाथि काठका तोरण राखिएका छन् । पूर्व, पश्चिम र उत्तरपट्टिका ढोकामाथि राखिएका तोरणहरूमा १८ हात भएकी महिषासुरमर्दिनी राखिएको छ भने दक्षिणपट्टिको ढोकामाथि राखिएको तोरणमा चामुण्डा राखिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र शिलाको पद्मपत्रमा सादा गोलाकार स्वरूपको यन्त्रलाई वत्सलाको रूपमा स्थापना गरिएको छ । वत्सलाका यन्त्रमुनि पञ्चदण्डीकेश्वर महादेव रहेको मानिन्छ (M. Thāpā VS 2077, p.479) ।यस मन्दिरको निर्माणसम्बन्धी ऐतिहासिक अभिलेख भेटिएको छैन । वंशावलीअनुसार गुह्येश्वरी पीठ प्रकट भएकै बेलादेखि पशुपति क्षेत्रमा वत्सलादेवी पनि विराजमान थिइन् । सूर्यवंशी राजा शिवदेवको पालामा कलिगत २८९५-९६ वैशाख शुक्ल ११ विहिवारको दिनमा नरबलि दिई विधिपूर्वक पद्माकार शिलाभित्र गुह्ययन्त्र प्रतिष्ठा गरी देवालय बनाइएको थियो । त्यसको दुई-तीन वर्षपछि पशुपतिनाथबाट काठमाडौंका भद्रकाली, कंकेश्वरी आदि देवीहरूलाई निमन्त्रणा गराई विधिपूर्वक नरबलि दिई नरशिवा (हातखुट्टाले टेकी स्याल जस्तै अभिनय गर्ने मानिस) हरूलाई कोलाहल गरी कराउन लगाई पूजा गर्ने प्रचलन चलाइएको थियो । शिवदेवपछिका पाँचौं पुस्ताका राजा विश्वगुप्तको पालामा कलिगत ३१८१ मा प्रतिवर्ष नरबलि चलाउन गार्‍हो हुनाले देवीलाई शान्ति पूजा गरी दुईवटा निखर बोका (अंगभंग नभएको कालो बोका) बलि दिने रीत चलाइदिए (Devamālāvaṃśāvalī2013, pp.36-37) । अर्को वंशावलीअनुसार राजा शिवदेववर्मनले नेपालका पीठमध्ये प्रमुख पीठ वत्सला हो भन्ने थाहा पाएर नरबलि दिने, त्रयोदशीको दिन कुमार-कुमारीहरूलाई भोजन गराउने र पिशाच चतुर्दशी (चैत्र कृष्ण १४) मा खटजात्रा गर्ने प्रचलन शुरु गरेका थिए (Nepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī2016, 12.136-137) । वंशावलीका यी कुराहरूलाई प्रमाणित गर्ने ऐतिहासिक सामग्री प्राप्त भएको छैन । वत्सला मन्दिरको उत्तरमा रहेको पञ्चगणेश मन्दिरको पछाडि भित्तामा एउटा ठूलो शिलालेख राखिएको छ । सम्भवत: यो लिच्छविकालीन अभिलेख हुनसक्छ । वत्सला मन्दिरसँग सम्बन्धित उक्त शिलालेखमा अहिले कुनै अक्षर बाँकी छैनन् । नेसं ७९५ (सन् १६७५) मा वत्सलादेवीको पर्वपूजा चलाउन ४५ रोपनीभन्दा बढी क्षेत्रफलको खेत गुठी राखिएको थियो (M. Panta VS 2055, pp.43-44) । प्रत्येक वर्ष चैत्र कृष्ण औंसीमा वत्सलालाई जाँडले स्नान गराउनको लागि विसं १८५२ (सन् १७९६) मा राजा रणबहादुर शाहले अर्नाका सिङ चढाएका थिए (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2056, p.290) । विसं १९६८ (सन् १९११) मा ठाकुरप्रसाद टंडन लाहुरी क्षेत्रीले पत्नीसँग मिलेर वत्सलालाई घण्टा चढाएका थिए (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2056, p.111) । विसं १९९० (सन् १९३४) को भूकम्पले मन्दिरका कुनै क्षति भएको थिएन (Devamālāvaṃśāvalī2013, p.37) । विसं २०७४ (सन् २०१७) मा पशुपति क्षेत्र विकास कोषसँगको सहकार्यमा चौधरी फाउण्डेशनद्वारा मन्दिरको मर्मत गरी रंगरोगन गरिएको थियो ।नेपालमाहात्म्यमा वत्सालाको महिमा उल्लेख गर्दै बागमतीमा स्नान गरी वत्सलाको दर्शनपूजन गर्नेहरूले कैलाशमा बास गर्न पाउँछन्, उनको भक्तिभाव गर्नाले सिद्धि प्राप्त हुन्छ भनिएको छ (Acharya 1992, p.19) । त्यसैले मानिसहरू भक्तिपूर्वक वत्सलाको पूजा गर्छन् । यस मन्दिरमा छुट्टै पुजारी नियुक्त गरिएको छैन । जयवागीश्वरी (PPK1222) का पुजारीले नै तान्त्रिक विधिले नित्यपूजा गरिरहेका छन् । द्य:पा:ला:को रूपमा खड्गी रहने परम्परा छ । चैत्र कृष्ण १४ का दिन वत्सला मन्दिरमाजा पाय्‌गु पूजागरिन्छ । त्यस पूजामा वत्सलाको पीठको मुख मात्रा देखिने गरी तीन पाठी चामलको भातले छोप्ने गरिन्छ र निखर कालो बोकाहरू बलि दिइन्छन् । त्यसै दिन राति कुमारी र कुमारहरूलाई चौरासी व्यञ्जन खुवाउने गरिन्छ । कुमारी र कुमारहरूलाई भोजन गराउँदा जम्बुद्वीपमा बालिएको आगोमा दुईवटा कालो बोका पोली प्रसाद स्वरूप वितरण गरिन्छ । चैत्र कृष्ण औंसीको दिन बिहान रणबहादुर शाहले चढाएको अर्नाको सिङबाट जाँडको धारा बगाई वत्सलालाई स्नान गराइन्छ । त्यसलाई स्थानीय भाषामाछाहाय्‌केगुभनिन्छ । त्यस स्नानबाट निस्कने जाँडको धारा बगेर टुटी (PPK0224-005) बाट झर्ने गर्छ । त्यस धाराबाट निस्केको जाँडलाई पवित्र मानी नुहाउनको लागि भक्तजनहरूको भीड लाग्छ । त्यसपछि ध्वं गुठीका एकजना गुठीयार स्यालको अनुकरण गरी तीनपटक कराउँछन् । ध्वं गुठीको लागि ३१ रोपनी १२ आना जग्गा गुठी राखिएको छ (Guṭhī Saṃsthāna VS 2071, p. 41) ।
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: Sources and references Inscription identification number PPK0224_I_001 Sources Stone inscription embedded to the east wall of the Pañcagaṇeśa Mandira. H: 159 cm, W: 33.2 cm.

historical_events.event_description: There is a large stone inscription set on the rear wall of the Pañcagaṇeśa Mandira, situated north of Vatsaleśvarī. This inscription, dating back to the Licchavi period, is now considerably eroded but is believed to be associated with the Vatsalā Mandira.

An extensive area of over 45ropanīs of land was endowed to set up a trust (guthi) responsible for conducting various rituals at the temple. The trust included Mānandhara (text: Manaṃdhra) Puna, Kṛṣṇa, Hṛdayasiṃha, Viṣṇusiṃha, and Harisiṃ as members. The income from the land was to be used for sacrificing a buffalo a day ahead ofPiśācaCaturdaśī, the 14th of the dark fortnight of Caitra, and lighting five sets of lamps at the Kvāthachẽ Āgaṃ. Additionally, the funds were utilized for the worship of Vatsalā on the new moon day of Caitra. Likewise, the trust was also responsible for sending the set of five nectars (pañcāmṛta) to Buṅgadyaḥ on the day of the deity’s ritual bathing (nhavaṃ), the 1st of the dark fortnight of Vaiśākha. The original donation deed was damaged in a fire and was copied into a new donation deed.

historical_events.event_name: Offering horn of wild water buffalo
historical_events.event_description: King Raṇabahādura Śāha offered three horns of wildarnābuffaloes for fermented beer (thvã) to be poured from it on to the stoneyantrarevered as Goddess Vatsalā on the new moon day of Caitra. Gold sheets were wrapped around the horns back then.

historical_events.event_name: Lālamohara by Raṇabahādura Śāha for Sindūra Guṭhī
historical_events.event_description: King Raṇabahādura Śāha, through a royal decree with a red seal (lālamohara), granted authorization to a trust named the Sindūra Guthi, allowing it to operate in accordance with the established tradition. King Jayaprakāśa Malla had endowed 120ropanīs of land for the trust of Goddess Vatsalā. Thelālamoharainstructed the trust members to perform thepañcopacāraworship, which involved offering a buffalo sacrifice to Vatsalā onPiśācaCaturdaśī, the 14th of the dark fortnight of Caitra. Additionally, during the same occasion, the horns of the wildarnābuffaloes were to be blown. Furthermore, the royal decree made the trust responsible for organizing thesindūrajātrāof Vatsalā on the new moon day of Caitra. Sixdhārnīs (1dhārnī= 2.39 kgs) of vermillion powder (sindūra) were required for the procession. Devotees participated the procession by throwing thesindūrapowder in the air and at each other, creating a vibrant atmosphere.
Ṭhākuraprasāda Ṭaṇḍana Lāhurī Kṣetrī and his wife offered a bell and 54 pieces of lamps to Vatsalā.

भतकुनि टोल (भकुंटोल) बस्ने कजि विष्णुदेवी र काजीमान दंगुले वत्सला मन्दिरमा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको पता: चढाएका थिए । काजीमान, तुलसीमान लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर अरु पनि केही वस्तु चढाएका थिए । अभिलेख स्पष्ट नभएकोले को भाव बुझ्न गार्‍हो छ ।
The Chaudhary Foundation in cooperation with the Pashupati Area Development Trust renovated the temple and furbished it with colors.

historical_events.event_description: The content of the inscription embossed on the temple's eaves board poses some challenges. It involves the names of Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā and his wife Siddhigajendralakṣmī, who happened to be the younger sister of his first wife. Following the passing of his first wife, Jaṅga Bahādura proposed marriage to Siddhigajendralakṣmī, but her father declined the proposal and instead married her to another man. After Jaṅga Bahādura took the office of the prime minister, he took Siddhigajendralakṣmī as his wife forcibly but paid her husband the compensation (P. Rāja VS 2073, p.57).

A family from the Dhaṃgu caste offered a narrow oblong banner (patāḥ) to the temple. The name of the donor and the year of the donation are not clearly visible. Only the name of the donor’s wife, Pāravati, can be read.
